attack_chain: Attacker submits a large number of comments (or very large payloads) via POST /comment (app.py:13)
COMMENTS list (app.py:8) grows unbounded, consuming excessive memory
GET /comments (app.py:19) or /admin/moderate (app.py:23) slows down or crashes due to memory exhaustion
Service becomes unavailable for all users

findings.failure_mode: Session Secret Key Leak via JavaScript Access
findings.trigger: Admin user visits /comments or /admin/moderate after a malicious comment with XSS payload is posted.
findings.business_impact: Full admin privilege escalation. Attacker can moderate/delete all comments, impersonate admins, and perform actions as authenticated admin. Business reputation damaged due to unauthorized moderation.
findings.blast_radius: All admin sessions are at risk. Compromised session allows access to /admin/moderate (Tier 1) and full control over COMMENTS (Tier 1). Lateral movement possible if admin sessions are reused across other systems.
attack_chain: Attacker crafts a malicious comment with embedded JavaScript (XSS payload) in the 'author' or 'body' field via POST /comment
Malicious comment is stored in COMMENTS list (app.py:13)
Victim admin views /comments or /admin/moderate, triggering template rendering (comments.html) which executes the XSS payload
XSS payload reads the session cookie (enabled by SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=False at app.py:7)
Attacker exfiltrates the session cookie to their server, hijacking the admin session

findings.failure_mode: Race Condition in COMMENTS List Corruption
findings.trigger: High-frequency concurrent POST /comment requests with large or malformed inputs.
findings.business_impact: Denial of service for all comment-related functionality. Admins cannot moderate, and users cannot view comments. Business operations relying on guestbook are disrupted.
findings.blast_radius: Affects all endpoints depending on COMMENTS (Tier 1): /comment, /comments, /admin/moderate. May cause Flask app crash (taking down all endpoints).
attack_chain: Attacker sends rapid concurrent POST /comment requests with malformed or oversized payloads
Flask's default thread-per-request model allows parallel writes to the in-memory COMMENTS list (app.py:8)
Race condition occurs during COMMENTS.append() (app.py:13), leading to list corruption or partial writes
Subsequent GET /comments or /admin/moderate requests crash due to malformed data in COMMENTS

findings.failure_mode: Stored XSS via Unvalidated Comment Input
findings.trigger: User submits a comment containing <script> tags or other HTML/JS, then any user views the comments page.
findings.business_impact: Arbitrary code execution in user browsers. Can lead to session hijacking (if HttpOnly=False), defacement, or phishing. Harms all users and admins viewing comments.
findings.blast_radius: All users and admins accessing /comments or /admin/moderate. Can spread to other domains if same-site cookies are used elsewhere.
attack_chain: Attacker submits a comment with HTML/JS payload in 'author' or 'body' via POST /comment (app.py:13)
Payload is stored unfiltered in COMMENTS list
When any user (including admins) views /comments or /admin/moderate, the template (comments.html) renders the payload as HTML
Malicious script executes in the victim's browser context

findings.failure_mode: Session Fixation Attack via Predictable Session Tokens
findings.trigger: Admin logs in while an attacker-controlled session cookie is already set in their browser.
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized admin access. Attacker can perform moderation actions, delete comments, or escalate privileges. Business integrity compromised.
findings.blast_radius: All admin sessions created without session regeneration. Affects /admin/moderate (Tier 1) and any session-dependent functionality.
attack_chain: Attacker sets a known session ID in the victim's browser (e.g., via a malicious link with ?session=attacker_known_id)
Victim logs in as admin (session['is_admin'] = True) without invalidating the existing session
Attacker uses the known session ID to access /admin/moderate (app.py:24-25) since Flask does not rotate session IDs on login
Attacker gains admin privileges without authentication

findings.failure_mode: SECRET_KEY Exposure via Environment Variable Leak
findings.trigger: SECRET_KEY is exposed through environment variable leakage (e.g., logs, process listings, or container images).
findings.business_impact: Complete authentication bypass. Attacker gains full admin control. Business data and user trust are severely compromised.
findings.blast_radius: All session-based authentication is broken. Affects /admin/moderate (Tier 1) and any endpoint relying on Flask sessions.
attack_chain: Attacker gains access to the host environment (e.g., via misconfigured cloud metadata, container escape, or insider threat)
Attacker reads the SECRET_KEY environment variable (app.py:6)
Attacker uses the SECRET_KEY to forge arbitrary Flask session cookies (e.g., setting is_admin=True)
Attacker bypasses authentication at /admin/moderate (app.py:24) by presenting the forged session

findings.failure_mode: Denial of Service via Memory Exhaustion (COMMENTS List Bloat)
findings.trigger: Sustained high-volume POST /comment requests with oversized inputs.
findings.business_impact: Full service outage. Business operations relying on the guestbook are halted. Reputation damage due to downtime.
findings.blast_radius: Entire Flask application (all Tier 1 and Tier 2 endpoints) becomes unavailable until restart.
attack_chain: Attacker sends repeated POST /comment requests with large payloads (e.g., 1GB 'body' strings)
COMMENTS list (app.py:8) grows unbounded in memory, consuming all available RAM
Flask app crashes due to OOM (Out of Memory) error, taking down all endpoints
All users and admins lose access to /comment, /comments, and /admin/moderate

findings.failure_mode: Privilege Escalation via Missing Authorization on /comments
findings.trigger: Any user (or automated scanner) accesses GET /comments.
findings.evidence: app.py:19 ("return render_template('comments.html', comments=COMMENTS)"), app.py:24 ("if not session.get('is_admin')")
findings.business_impact: Information disclosure. Sensitive or unmoderated comments may be exposed to unauthorized users. Business confidentiality violated.
findings.blast_radius: All comments (Tier 1) are exposed. May enable further attacks (e.g., XSS) if unmoderated comments contain payloads.
attack_chain: Attacker notes that GET /comments (app.py:19) has no access control (unlike /admin/moderate at app.py:24)
Attacker uses /comments to enumerate all comments, including those pending moderation
If comments contain sensitive data (e.g., admin notes), attacker gains unauthorized access
No direct escalation, but information disclosure aids further attacks (e.g., crafting targeted XSS)

findings.failure_mode: Stored XSS leading to admin session hijack
findings.trigger: Admin visits /comments or /admin/moderate after attacker submits XSS payload in comment body
findings.business_impact: Full admin account compromise. Attacker can delete/modify all comments, access admin-only functions, and perform actions as admin. Business reputation damaged, user trust eroded.
findings.blast_radius: All admin sessions are at risk. Compromise of admin auth affects all moderation capabilities and could enable further attacks on the system.
attack_chain: Attacker posts a comment with malicious JavaScript in the 'body' field via POST /comment
Malicious script is stored in the global COMMENTS list (app.py:13)
When admin views /comments or /admin/moderate, comments.html renders the script (app.py:19,26)
Script executes in admin's browser, stealing session cookie (non-HTTP-only, app.py:7)
Attacker uses stolen session cookie to impersonate admin

findings.failure_mode: Session fixation / privilege escalation via SECRET_KEY exposure
findings.trigger: Exposure of SECRET_KEY environment variable (e.g., via logs, process listing, or misconfigured deployment)
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized admin access. Attacker can moderate/delete all comments, disrupt service, and perform privileged actions. Business operations compromised.
findings.blast_radius: All session-based authentication is broken. Any user with the SECRET_KEY can forge admin sessions.
attack_chain: Attacker gains access to SECRET_KEY (e.g., via env leak, logs, or misconfiguration)
Attacker crafts a session cookie with is_admin=True using the known SECRET_KEY
Attacker sets this cookie in their browser and accesses /admin/moderate
Server validates session (app.py:24) and grants admin access

findings.failure_mode: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion (COMMENTS list)
findings.trigger: Rapid, high-volume POST requests to /comment with large or numerous payloads
findings.business_impact: Service outage for all users and admins. No comments can be viewed or moderated until restart. Business downtime and potential financial loss.
findings.blast_radius: Entire application becomes unavailable. Adjacent systems relying on this service may also fail.
attack_chain: Attacker sends repeated POST requests to /comment with large payloads (e.g., 1GB 'body' strings)
Each request appends to the global COMMENTS list (app.py:13)
Memory usage grows unbounded as COMMENTS list expands
Server runs out of memory, crashing the Flask process

findings.failure_mode: Unauthorized comment deletion/modification via missing auth on /comments
findings.trigger: Direct manipulation of client-side requests to /comments or template-based actions
findings.evidence: app.py:17-19 ("GET /comments exposes all comments without access control")
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized modification or deletion of user-generated content. Loss of data integrity, user frustration, and potential legal/compliance issues.
findings.blast_radius: All comments are at risk of tampering. No audit trail or recovery mechanism exists.
attack_chain: Attacker observes that GET /comments (app.py:17-19) exposes all comments without access control
Attacker crafts a request to modify/delete comments by exploiting the lack of validation in the template or backend
If comments.html template allows client-side manipulation (e.g., via hidden forms), attacker submits malicious requests

findings.failure_mode: Race condition in COMMENTS list leading to comment corruption
findings.trigger: High concurrency of POST /comment requests (e.g., during traffic spikes)
findings.business_impact: Data corruption in comment history. Users may lose comments or see inconsistent data. Business reputation harmed due to unreliable service.
findings.blast_radius: All comments in the COMMENTS list may be affected. Moderation and display functions break.
attack_chain: Multiple users submit comments concurrently via POST /comment
Global COMMENTS list (app.py:8) is modified without thread-safety (Flask runs in multi-threaded mode by default)
Race condition causes comments to be lost, duplicated, or corrupted in the list

findings.failure_mode: Session cookie theft via MITM (non-HTTPS + non-HTTP-only)
findings.trigger: User accesses the site over an unencrypted (HTTP) connection on a compromised network
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized access to user and admin accounts. Sensitive actions performed by attackers. Loss of trust and potential regulatory penalties.
findings.blast_radius: All active sessions are vulnerable. If admin session is stolen, full system compromise is possible.
attack_chain: Attacker sets up a MITM position (e.g., on shared WiFi or compromised network)
User visits the site over HTTP (implied by lack of HTTPS enforcement)
Session cookie is sent in plaintext (non-HTTP-only, app.py:7) and intercepted by attacker
Attacker hijacks the user's session, including admin sessions if stolen

findings.failure_mode: Privilege escalation via session tampering (is_admin flag manipulation)
findings.trigger: Attacker modifies their session cookie to include is_admin=True and re-signs it with the SECRET_KEY
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized admin access. Attacker can perform privileged actions, disrupt service, and compromise data integrity.
findings.blast_radius: All session-based authentication is at risk. Any user can escalate privileges if SECRET_KEY is compromised or weak.
attack_chain: Attacker logs in as a regular user, obtaining a session cookie
Attacker decodes the Flask session cookie (signed with SECRET_KEY) and modifies the is_admin flag to True
If SECRET_KEY is weak or known, attacker re-signs the cookie and sets it in their browser
Attacker accesses /admin/moderate, bypassing the check (app.py:24)
